learner_operation: Independently recall indexing convention, select the requested row and column, and enter one displayed integer.

fixed_features.feature: 2x2 integer matrix; one valid named entry; one mathematical blank.
fixed_features.justification: Explicit target scope and endpoint, not incidental source parameters.

fixed_features.feature: Unguided prompt and row-then-column worked solution.
fixed_features.justification: Preserves required recall and selection before feedback; tutorial support does not migrate into independent prompts.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: a_11, a_12, a_21, a_22 supported by fixture-q11/q12/q21/q22.
answer_roles.observed: Anchors request a_12, a_21, a_12. Only off-diagonal positions happen to be illustrated; no diagonal prohibition follows.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Any integer, including positive, negative or zero; no magnitude quota in source.
answer_roles.observed: -3, -31, 307; signs and digit lengths vary, but no source-supported requirement to place zero or all positions among exactly three design anchors.

coverage.result: Original easy fixture-q12 retained mathematically, including its negative single-digit result. It still requires recalling the index convention and locating row 1, column 2 without help.

Compared with easy, two-digit signed integers add a modest transcription demand. Selecting row 2, column 1 still requires precisely the same recall and two location decisions. The moderate label is authored and uncalibrated, with no extra arithmetic.

Compared with moderate, three-digit integers add only a modest reading/transcription demand. Selecting row 1, column 2 still uses identical reasoning and one blank. The hard label is authored and uncalibrated; no added matrix operation or conversion is justified or present.

counterfactuals.change: Replace the selected value by its successor independently in each anchor.
counterfactuals.expected: Each lookup response changes to the replacement integer.
counterfactuals.observed: All three changes produce the expected new value.
counterfactuals.justification: Direct application of the taught entry-reading rule; these are mathematical witnesses and not runtime generator claims.

counterfactuals.change: Increment a different cell, leaving the requested cell unchanged, independently in each anchor.
counterfactuals.expected: Each lookup response remains the original selected integer.
counterfactuals.observed: All three changes preserve the original result.
counterfactuals.justification: Direct application of the taught entry-reading rule; these are mathematical witnesses and not runtime generator claims.

shortcut_applicability.reason: Inspect visible cell styling and simple positional/value cues on this finite anchor set. Multiple-choice bank/rank probes are inapplicable to a free-entry endpoint.

shortcut_probes.cue: Always read the upper-right cell without interpreting the requested indices.
shortcut_probes.subgroup: All three design anchors, both raw and delivered identities.
shortcut_probes.strategy: Read top-right value only; omit a_ij interpretation.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Succeeds on 2/3: fails on moderate a_21. This is diagnostic only; it establishes no recurring generator defect or shortcut-free population.

shortcut_probes.cue: Choose the numerically smallest matrix value without locating the target.
shortcut_probes.strategy: Inspect the four integers and output their minimum, ignoring the indices.
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Succeeds on 2/3: fails on hard. Uniform cell styling and the absence of row/column markers show no direct prompt annotation that supplies the answer. Counts are diagnostic, not proof about an unseen generator.

delivery.result: All three raw anchors yield one survivor each. Mathematical values, target indices, support and response demands are preserved by normalization. This is offline preparation only.

limitations: One fixed anchor per band cannot establish generator distribution, all-cell coverage or resistance to every shortcut.
No generator, rejection/resampling, learner history, weighted selection, refill or publication was admitted or tested.
Moderate/hard progression is an authored modest integer-reading demand; all original cases are easy.
Probe baseline 0.25 describes uniformly guessing one of four distinct displayed entries for these anchors; it is not a population estimate.
